2
A crane has an arm to which is attached a frictionless pulley. A cable passes over the pulley and
supports a load of 10 kN as shown.
F
10 kN
frictionless pulley
30°
30°
crane arm
load
10 kN
The crane arm exerts a force F on the pulley.
What is the value of F ?
A
5.0 kN
B
8.7 kN
C
10 kN
D
17 kN

hints: Notice the cable has $10\text{ kN}$ tension on both sides of the frictionless pulley, one vertical and one at $30^{\circ}$ to the crane arm.
Connect this to equilibrium of the pulley: $F$ must balance the vector sum, which acts along the angle bisector, i.e. along the crane arm with each tension at $30^{\circ}$ to $F$.
Resolve each $10\text{ kN}$ force along the direction of $F$ using $10\cos30^{\circ}$ and add the two parallel components.
walkthrough: The frictionless pulley means tension is the same throughout the cable, so the pulley is pulled by two $10\text{ kN}$ forces: one vertically down to the load and one along the left cable.
From the diagram each $10\text{ kN}$ force makes $30^{\circ}$ with the crane arm. By symmetry the resultant of the two pulls acts along the arm, opposite to $F$.
For equilibrium of the light pulley, $F$ equals the magnitude of that resultant. Resolve each tension along the arm direction: component $= 10\cos30^{\circ}$.
This gives $F \approx 17.3\text{ kN}$, about $17\text{ kN}$ with correct units of force. This is option D.

A.explanation: Too small because it halves a single $10\text{ kN}$ tension instead of adding the two $10\text{ kN}$ pulls along the arm direction.

B.explanation: This is the component of only one $10\text{ kN}$ cable pull along $F$, given by $10\cos30^{\circ}$, and it omits the second side of the cable.

C.explanation: Incorrect because the two $10\text{ kN}$ forces are at $60^{\circ}$ to each other, not opposite, so their vector sum is larger than $10\text{ kN}$.

D.explanation: Correct because $F$ balances the vector sum of the two $10\text{ kN}$ tensions, giving $2 \times 10\cos30^{\circ} \approx 17\text{ kN}$.
